Both direct "add selection to library" paths (the keyboard/context-menu action and the drag-onto-sidebar action in `LibraryMenu.tsx`) now route through `mergeLibraryItems`, and `isUniqueItem` itself now compares elements by normalized structural content instead of by volatile `id`/`versionNonce`.

## Summary

Root cause had two parts in `packages/excalidraw/data/library.ts`:

1. **`isUniqueItem` compared elements by `id`/`versionNonce`** — random, instance-specific identifiers that differ across documents/sessions even for a visually identical shape, and even across two reloads of the same content in some code paths. Replaced it with `getComparableLibraryItemElements`, which strips volatile fields (`id`, `version`, `versionNonce`, `seed`, `updated`, `index`) and normalizes id-based cross-references (`groupIds`, `frameId`, `boundElements`, `containerId`, `startBinding`/`endBinding`) to positions within the item itself, then compares elements by stable, sorted-key content. Element count and array order are still compared positionally, so items differing only in shape count or stacking order remain distinct.

2. **`actionAddToLibrary.ts` and `LibraryMenu.tsx`'s "add to library" flow bypassed dedup entirely**, calling `library.setLibrary()` with a raw prepended item instead of going through `mergeLibraryItems`. Any item added this way — including a literal duplicate of an already-existing item — was never checked against the existing library at all. Both now build the new item and merge it via `mergeLibraryItems`.

## Summary

**Root cause:** `isUniqueItem` in `packages/excalidraw/data/library.ts` deduplicated library items by comparing each element's `id` and `versionNonce` — both are randomly generated per element *instance*, not derived from its visual content. So two shapes that are pixel-for-pixel identical but were created independently (a different import of the same library, a shape that arrived via another document/session, or a re-export) always get fresh random ids/versionNonce and therefore never compared equal, even though nothing about their appearance differs. That's why the existing dedup logic "caught none" of the reported cases.

- strips purely random/volatile per-instance fields (`id`, `seed`, `version`, `versionNonce`, `updated`, `index`),

- still compares elements by array order and requires equal element counts up front, so items differing only in stacking order or in how many shapes they contain remain distinct.

`mergeLibraryItems`/`isUniqueItem` now use this signature for equality instead of raw id/versionNonce matching.

I also added tests in `packages/excalidraw/tests/library.test.tsx` covering: re-adding identical content is deduped, genuinely different content is still added, different element counts are treated as different, and different stacking order is treated as different.

## Summary

**Root cause:** `isUniqueItem` in `packages/excalidraw/data/library.ts` treated two library items as duplicates only if their elements matched by `id` **and** `versionNonce`, index by index. Both fields are randomly (re)generated per authoring session — they get regenerated on export/re-publish, and are naturally different when the same-looking shape was created independently in another document/session. So this identity check almost never matched in the real-world scenarios described (re-adding a library, reopening a `.excalidrawlib`, items arriving via another route), and every item got re-added.

**Fix:** Replaced the identity-based check with a content-based signature per element (`getElementContentSignature`) that ignores identity/reference-only fields (`id`, `seed`, `version`, `versionNonce`, `updated`, `groupIds`, `frameId`, `boundElements`, `containerId`, and the `elementId` inside bindings) while keeping everything that affects how the element looks/behaves. `mergeLibraryItems` now compares items by the join of their elements' signatures, so:
- Identical-looking items are recognized as duplicates regardless of origin.
- Items with a different element count or different signature per element are still distinct.
- Reordering elements (different stacking) changes the joined signature, so stacking-order differences are still preserved as distinct items.
